name: binary search with no array
hook: Binary search needs a sorted array. This problem has none, and binary search still solves it: {binary_checks} checks instead of {brute_checks}.
hook_sub: Nothing is sorted. So search the answers instead.
caption: Koko eats bananas at k per hour, one pile at a time, and has h hours. Find the minimum k that finishes in time.

There is no sorted array here. But a faster speed never takes more hours, so every speed below the answer fails and every speed from it up works. The answers themselves are sorted: no, no, no, yes, yes, yes.
Trying every speed from 1 upward on piles of up to {big_max} bananas takes {brute_checks} checks. Binary search over the speeds takes {binary_checks}, and lands on the same {big_answer}.
Three signals that it applies: you are asked for a minimum value that satisfies a condition, you can check a candidate, and once a candidate works, every larger one does.
Which problem taught you this one? 👇

slides.h: The slowest speed that still finishes
p: Koko eats `k` bananas an hour, one pile at a time, and has `h` hours. Find the minimum `k`.

slides.h: Nothing here is sorted. The answers are.
p: A faster speed never takes more hours. So every speed below the answer fails, and every speed from it up works.
You are asked for a *minimum value* that satisfies a condition.
You can *check a candidate*: here, add up the hours at that speed.
Feasibility is *monotonic*: once a speed works, every faster one does.
